title: Newton–Girard in arbitrary arity, as a formal identity
content: The open question asks for the full Newton–Girard recurrence $p_k = \sum_i (-1)^{i-1} e_i p_{k-i}$ expressing power sums through elementary symmetric polynomials, for *any* number of variables. A gallery sibling proved the three-variable case by hand; this entry instead packages Mathlib's general development over $\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$ for any `Fintype σ` and commutative ring $R$. The key conceptual point is that these are *formal/combinatorial* identities in the polynomial ring — not facts about complex roots — so they hold over $\mathbb{Z}$, any commutative ring, and any finite variable set, with 0 axioms.
mathContext: $p_k = \sum_i (-1)^{i-1} e_i\, p_{k-i}$ as an identity in $\mathrm{MvPolynomial}\,\sigma\,R$.

title: The eₖ recurrence (k·eₖ from lower-degree data)
content: `newton_esymm_recurrence` states $k\cdot e_k = (-1)^{k+1}\sum_{i+j=k,\,i<k}(-1)^i e_i p_j$, expressing $k\,e_k$ through strictly lower-degree elementary symmetric polynomials and power sums. The summation ranges over the antidiagonal $\{(i,j): i+j=k\}$ filtered to $i<k$, which is the exact bookkeeping of the cross terms $e_i p_{k-i}$. In Lean this is a one-line wrapper around Mathlib's `mul_esymm_eq_sum`, itself proved by a sign-reversing (Zeilberger-style) involution on pairs.

title: The power-sum recurrence — the open question's target
content: `newton_psum_recurrence` is the OQ's target in full generality: for $k>0$, $p_k = (-1)^{k+1}k\,e_k - \sum_{i+j=k,\,0<i<k}(-1)^i e_i p_j$, the recurrence that computes every power sum from the elementary symmetric polynomials and the lower power sums. It is the solved-for-$p_k$ rearrangement of the $e_k$ recurrence, with the antidiagonal filter now $0<i<k$ excluding both endpoints. Wrapping Mathlib's `psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum`, it holds over any finite index type and any commutative ring.

title: Termination at k = number of variables
content: `newton_sum_zero` records that when $k$ reaches $|\sigma|$ (the number of variables), the full alternating sum $\sum_{i+j=k}(-1)^i e_i p_j$ vanishes. Beyond degree $|\sigma|$ the elementary symmetric polynomials are identically zero, so the recurrence terminates there: it is exactly the structural reason the roots↔coefficients dictionary is finite. This is the multivariate generalization of the fact that a degree-$n$ characteristic polynomial has only $n+1$ coefficients.

title: The base case p₁ = e₁
content: `psum_one_eq_esymm_one` proves $p_1 = e_1$ — both equal $\sum_i X_i$, the sum of the variables. This is the seed that, together with `newton_psum_recurrence`, computes every power sum from the elementary symmetric polynomials by induction on $k$. The proof is the one-liner `rw [psum_one, esymm_one]`. Without a base case the recurrence would determine the $p_k$ only up to the $k=1$ datum; supplying it makes the whole power-sum sequence explicit.
prerequisites: first power sum and first symmetric polynomial
